tested_scope: Authoritative GitHub REST documentation for repository Contents create/update semantics, general REST conditional-request rules, Git reference create/update semantics, and response request-id exposure; no remote mutation was used for the semantic test.

authoritative_public_sources.observation: Create-or-update contents documents Accept as the request header, message/content as required body fields, and sha only when updating an existing file; it documents 200/201/404/409/422 outcomes but no client idempotency key, immutable request token, If-Match/If-None-Match create precondition, or request-result replay primitive for the endpoint.

GitHub documents conditional requests primarily for GET and states that conditional requests for unsafe methods such as POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE are unsupported unless the specific endpoint documentation says otherwise.

Create-reference documents only ref and sha with 201/409/422; update-reference documents sha and force. These operations expose collision/fast-forward semantics but no client idempotency key or immutable request identity, and refs are explicitly rewritable.

X-GitHub-Request-Id is shown as response metadata. The reviewed documentation does not define it as a client-supplied idempotency key or a lookup/replay handle that can recover an unknown write outcome.

slice_result.observation: Within the exact reviewed transport semantics, no documented server-side primitive provides durable request identity or conditional create sufficient to distinguish never-applied from applied-but-response-lost create after later path/history loss. Optimistic sha checks protect updates, same-name creation can collide while the target exists, and request IDs aid response tracing, but none supplies an independently durable idempotency/replay record for the allowed Contents write path.
slice_result.supported_property: Update CAS and extant-target create collision remain useful bounded protections when current target state is observable.
slice_result.unresolved_boundary: Ambiguous create reconciliation remains dependent on observing retained target/history or another independent durable record. Prior role-local evidence already established that unprotected retained history is not an invariant under ref/history rewrite and unreachable-object pruning, so the reviewed server semantics do not close duplicate/conflict safety or ABA resistance.
slice_result.hard_gate_resolution: negative boundary evidence for server-side idempotency/request-identity/conditional-create rescue; full duplicate/conflict hard gate remains unresolved
